[MUQATIL:12:31-33/r2] MUQATIL, d. 150 · author | holds | Zulaykha told the women Joseph was the one they blamed her for desiring; he refused intercourse, so she threatened to imprison and disgrace him.
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابإضافةالمنقوصإلىالياءالتيهيعلامةالمجروروالمضمر)#595/r1] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | When a possessive yāʾ follows a final alif, the alif remains and is opened to avoid two adjacent vowelless consonants, as in بشراى and هداى.
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابإضافةالمنقوصإلىالياءالتيهيعلامةالمجروروالمضمر)#595/r2] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | reports | Some Arabs instead turn the ending into yāʾ in بشري and هدي, clarifying because both alif and yāʾ are weak or indistinct.
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابإضافةالمنقوصإلىالياءالتيهيعلامةالمجروروالمضمر)#595/r3] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | reports | Some pronounce أفعى with a final alif only in pause, while others retain it in connected speech too and treat it as a fixed yāʾ.
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالكافالتيهيعلامةالمضمر)#743/r1] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | The second-person pronominal kāf is kasra-marked for feminine and open for masculine, as is the second-person tāʾ.
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالكافالتيهيعلامةالمضمر)#743/r2] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | reports | Some Tamīm and Asad speakers replace feminine kāf with shīn in pause to distinguish gender more clearly, choosing a voiceless consonant near kāf in articulation.
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالكافالتيهيعلامةالمضمر)#743/r3] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | reports | Some Arabs append sīn after feminine kāf to clarify its kasra in pause, but drop it in connected speech because the vowel suffices.
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالكافالتيهيعلامةالمضمر)#743/r4] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | reports | Other speakers append shīn to the feminine kāf in pause for the same clarification and omit it when connecting speech.
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالكافالتيهيعلامةالمضمر)#743/r5] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | reports | Some speakers add alif after masculine kāf and yāʾ after feminine kāf before pronominal hāʾ, to make gender clearer in pause.
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالكافالتيهيعلامةالمضمر)#743/r6] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · الخليل | reports | Al-Khalīl reports the rare form ضربتيه with an added yāʾ; Sībawayh regards omission of the long vowel after kāf as the better and more common dialect.
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالكافالتيهيعلامةالمضمر)#743/r7] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | Long vowels are added to light hāʾ more readily than to kāf or tāʾ because hāʾ is weak, like alif.
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالنونالثقيلةوالخفيفة)#640/r1] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · الخليل | reports | Al-Khalīl says both emphatic nūns add emphasis, with the heavy form stronger than the light one.
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالنونالثقيلةوالخفيفة)#640/r10] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | The interrogative pattern is attested by al-Aʿshā's أن يأتين, Muqanniʿ's تمدحن, and another example هل تحنفن, identified as light nūn.
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالنونالثقيلةوالخفيفة)#640/r11] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · يونس | reports | Yūnus permits emphatic nūn after هلا and ألا in interrogative forms.
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالنونالثقيلةوالخفيفة)#640/r12] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | prefers | Sībawayh considers Yūnus's analysis apt because these forms invite or urge the addressee, much like a command; لولا works similarly.
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالنونالثقيلةوالخفيفة)#640/r14] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | Without intervening ما, nūn occurs rarely in conditional clauses in poetry by analogy with jussive, nonassertive prohibitions; Sībawayh says it is licensed only by poetic necessity.
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالنونالثقيلةوالخفيفة)#640/r15] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | Ibn al-Khurʿ's مهما clauses and anonymous poetic examples attest emphatic nūn in conditional forms; the usage is stronger within conditionals than elsewhere.
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالنونالثقيلةوالخفيفة)#640/r16] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | In أقسمت لما لم تفعلن, the request makes the construction behave like a prohibition and licenses emphatic nūn.
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالنونالثقيلةوالخفيفة)#640/r17] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | Emphatic nūn occurs with nonassertive expressions such as بجهد ما تبلغن because of the particle ما, as in cited proverbs.
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالنونالثقيلةوالخفيفة)#640/r18] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | A normally indicative verb can take nūn only under poetic necessity, by analogy with interrogatives; Sībawayh gives this rule for the form أنت تفعلن.
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالنونالثقيلةوالخفيفة)#640/r19] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | Jadhīma al-Abrash's line ربما أوفيت في علم ترفعن ثوبي شمالات illustrates emphatic nūn on an indicative verb under metrical necessity.
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالنونالثقيلةوالخفيفة)#640/r2] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | A nonassertive verb governed by an oath lām must carry either the heavy or light emphatic nūn; 12:32 illustrates both forms.
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالنونالثقيلةوالخفيفة)#640/r20] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · يونس | reports | Yūnus reports emphatic nūn after ربما and كثر ما because the verbs are nonassertive and the particles are followed by ما.
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالنونالثقيلةوالخفيفة)#640/r21] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | prefers | Sībawayh says omission is more common and better here: unlike oath lām, these particles do not require nūn, while lām prevents confusion with negation.
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالنونالثقيلةوالخفيفة)#640/r22] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | prefers | With حيثما, nūn is possible in the conditional, but omission is better because حيث and ما function as one particle, unlike oath lām.
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالنونالثقيلةوالخفيفة)#640/r3] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | Sībawayh identifies the first nūn in the threat as heavy and the nūn in the following verb as light.
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالنونالثقيلةوالخفيفة)#640/r5] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | Supplication behaves like command and prohibition; Ibn Rawāḥa's prayer uses the heavy emphatic nūn.
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالنونالثقيلةوالخفيفة)#640/r7] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | Al-Aʿshā's line demonstrates heavy nūn in لا تقربنها and light nūn in فاعبدا.
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالنونالثقيلةوالخفيفة)#640/r8] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | Poetic attestations include Zuhayr's light تعلمن, al-Aʿshā's light لا تعلقنك, al-Nābigha al-Dhubyānī's لا أعرفن and فلتأتينك, and al-Nābigha al-Jaʿdī's light لأثأرا.
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالنونالثقيلةوالخفيفة)#640/r9] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | Nūn is also optional with nonassertive verbs after interrogative particles, since the question can mean ‘inform me’; Sībawayh cites poetic examples.
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماكانعلىحرفينوليستفيهعلامةالتأنيث)#659/r1] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | Nouns originally triliteral but reduced to two letters form paucal plurals on أفعل, as in يد and أيد.
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماكانعلىحرفينوليستفيهعلامةالتأنيث)#659/r10] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | Some two-letter feminine nouns take only a tāʾ plural; tāʾ can also be added where wāw and nūn plurals exist because it is the basic suffix.
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماكانعلىحرفينوليستفيهعلامةالتأنيث)#659/r11] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | When a broken plural restores the deleted consonant, speakers may leave off sound suffixes, as in شفة/شفاه and شاة/شياه.
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماكانعلىحرفينوليستفيهعلامةالتأنيث)#659/r12] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | أمة has plurals آم and إماء, analogous to أكمة/آكم/إكام; the restored form makes إمون and أمات unnecessary.
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماكانعلىحرفينوليستفيهعلامةالتأنيث)#659/r13] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | The plural آم is analyzed on the feminine faʿla pattern because comparable intact nouns use أفعل; the restored plural makes إمون and أمات unnecessary.
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماكانعلىحرفينوليستفيهعلامةالتأنيث)#659/r14] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | The variants برة/برات/برون/بري and لغة/لغى illustrate that speakers may use one plural pattern as a substitute or use several.
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماكانعلىحرفينوليستفيهعلامةالتأنيث)#659/r15] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · الخليل | reports | Al-Khalīl explains that أرضات is heavy because أرض is feminine and its tāʾ plural parallels forms such as طلحات and صفحات.
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماكانعلىحرفينوليستفيهعلامةالتأنيث)#659/r16] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | reports | In Sībawayh's dialogue, al-Khalīl relates أرضون to سنين because أرض is feminine like سنة; speakers use wāw and nūn rather than a broken plural.
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماكانعلىحرفينوليستفيهعلامةالتأنيث)#659/r17] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | reports | Al-Khalīl says أرض takes both tāʾ and wāw-nūn plurals, while أهل is masculine and does not take tāʾ or undergo that stem change.
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماكانعلىحرفينوليستفيهعلامةالتأنيث)#659/r18] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · يونس | reports | Yūnus reports حرة/حرون by analogy with feminine أرض/أرضون; the initial change in أرضين reflects a change already made medially.
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماكانعلىحرفينوليستفيهعلامةالتأنيث)#659/r19] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · يونس | reports | Yūnus also reports حرة/إحرون, treating it as a plural of an otherwise unattested إحرة form.
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماكانعلىحرفينوليستفيهعلامةالتأنيث)#659/r2] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | Their larger plurals may use فعال or فعول; lost consonants are restored, as in دماء and دمي.
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماكانعلىحرفينوليستفيهعلامةالتأنيث)#659/r20] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | Feminine nouns without tāʾ may take tāʾ plurals, including عرسات and أرضات; Hudhayl's pattern also changes the yāʾ in عيرات, like بيضات and جوازات.
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماكانعلىحرفينوليستفيهعلامةالتأنيث)#659/r21] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | سماء is pluralized as سموات for ‘sky’, with tāʾ serving in place of broken plural, as in عير and أرض.
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماكانعلىحرفينوليستفيهعلامةالتأنيث)#659/r22] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | أهل may have light or heavy أهلات; al-Mukhabbal al-Saʿdī attests أهلات in poetry.
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماكانعلىحرفينوليستفيهعلامةالتأنيث)#659/r23] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | أمة also has إموان, analogized to إخوان; al-Qattāl al-Kilābī's verse attests الأموان.
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماكانعلىحرفينوليستفيهعلامةالتأنيث)#659/r24] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | Al-Mukhabbal al-Saʿdī's أ

[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماكانعلىحرفينوليستفيهعلامةالتأنيث)#659/r4] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | reports | Sībawayh reports Yūnus's plural أخاء for أخ; he then cites إخوان on the pattern of خرب/خربان.

[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماكانعلىحرفينوليستفيهعلامةالتأنيث)#659/r8] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | Examples such as هنة/هنات and فئة/فئات retain their shape with tāʾ, while سنوات and عضوات restore the original form.
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماكانعلىحرفينوليستفيهعلامةالتأنيث)#659/r9] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | Adding wāw and nūn to feminine stems can trigger an initial change, as in سنون and ثبون, because that masculine suffix is not native to them.
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابنفيالفعل)#495/r1] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | A simple perfect فعل is negated with لم يفعل.
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابنفيالفعل)#495/r2] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | A perfect with قد فعل is negated with لما يفعل.
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابنفيالفعل)#495/r3] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | A perfect with لقد فعل is negated with ما فعل, matching an oath: والله لقد فعل / والله ما فعل.
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابنفيالفعل)#495/r4] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | For هو يفعل describing an action in progress, the negation is ما يفعل.
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابنفيالفعل)#495/r5] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | For هو يفعل when the action has not yet occurred, the negation is لا يفعل.
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابنفيالفعل)#495/r6] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | A verb with oath lām, ليفعلن, is negated with لا يفعل, again treating the lām as an oath.
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابنفيالفعل)#495/r7] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | A future with سوف يفعل is negated with لن يفعل.
[SIBAWAYH:وليسبمنادىينبههغيرهولكنهاختصكماأنالمنادىمختصمنPageV02P231#321/r1] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | Specialization is not a vocative used to summon someone; it singles out a person or group for a command, prohibition, or statement.
[SIBAWAYH:وليسبمنادىينبههغيرهولكنهاختصكماأنالمنادىمختصمنPageV02P231#321/r2] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | Specialization places the construction on the vocative particle, just as equivalence places a non-question on an interrogative particle.
[SIBAWAYH:وليسبمنادىينبههغيرهولكنهاختصكماأنالمنادىمختصمنPageV02P231#321/r3] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | Forms such as أما أنا ... أيها الرجل specify rather than leave the addressee vague; the vocative can reinforce a specification already made by أنا.
[SIBAWAYH:وليسبمنادىينبههغيرهولكنهاختصكماأنالمنادىمختصمنPageV02P231#321/r4] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | The particle يا is omitted because the speaker is not calling out to alert someone else.

[MAJAZ:v1p310/r7] MAJAZ, d. 209 · author | holds | An anonymous poem uses rabb for the owner of a herd.
[MAJAZ:v1p310/r8] MAJAZ, d. 209 · author | holds | Al-Aʿshā's poem names al-Nuʿmān as rabb; anshada means he gave when asked in written petitions.

[TAB-FULL:v13p141#2/r1] TAB-FULL, d. 310 · author | holds | The Aziz’s wife says the women’s loss of reason and cutting their hands after seeing Yusuf is exactly what they had blamed her for in loving him; she admits she pursued him and he resisted.

[BAQILLANI:v1p219/r4] BAQILLANI, d. 403 · author | prefers | Asked to choose, Bāqillānī defers to al-Buḥturī’s own judgment because a poet knows his poetry better than others.
